context:
Make the wheel/tooling boundary structural. After this TODO, contributors
installing benchbox in dev mode no longer pick up `jsonschema` or
`ruamel-yaml` transitively - those live in the isolated tooling env and
are only resolved when a TODO/release script is actually invoked.

Pattern reference: `uv` supports per-directory pyproject.toml resolution
via `--project`. Alternative is a tiny shim: `_project/scripts/run.sh`
that wraps `uv run --project $(dirname "$0") "$@"`.
description:
Internal TODO/release tooling under `_project/scripts/` is the structural
reason `jsonschema` lives in `[project] dependencies` and `ruamel-yaml`
lives in `[dependency-groups] dev`. These packages are not part of the
shipped wheel - `_project/` is excluded from packaging.

Audited tooling-only imports today:
  - `_project/scripts/validate_todo.py` → `jsonschema`
  - `_project/scripts/todo_cli.py` → `ruamel.yaml`

The interim fix in Phase 0 (`move-jsonschema-out-of-core-runtime-deps`)
shifts `jsonschema` from core to dev. That removes it from end-user
installs but keeps it in every contributor's dev env. The structural
fix is to give `_project/scripts/` its own `pyproject.toml` so the
boundary between "ships in the wheel" and "internal tooling" is
enforced by tooling, not by convention.

Source: `docs/development/dependency-inventory.md` findings F2 +
consolidation note on `_project/` being out of the public manifest.
